cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T3's gift claim directly; T8 picks up T7's scripts; T10 takes up T9's handover.
cells.limitation: T5 pivots to a new reading instead of answering T4's point that the gift no longer feels free.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5/T6 introduce reassurance-versus-workload, absent from openings; T7 builds two scripts on it.
cells.limitation: T11 largely returns to T3's opening anti-ledger stance, adding only one condition.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Gift versus fairness (T3, T4) and reassurance versus workload (T5, T6) are both examined.
cells.limitation: The friend's own view of the friendship, whether she sees it as lopsided, is never considered.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T10 narrows to handover first; T11 holds one point; disagreement remains open in D.
cells.limitation: The Maintenance Realist's handover (T9) is never challenged or reshaped by the other minds.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: D turns a yes/no question into two distinct worries plus a testable handover.
cells.limitation: T8's question about accepting a no is dropped from the final map in E.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T8 fairly grants the script is gentle, then uses Rosenberg's own request-demand distinction against it.
cells.limitation: T4 trims T3's gift view to a feeling, skipping T3's natural-host point.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 names the assumption a gift is freely given and says asking shows it no longer is.
cells.limitation: T9's claim that stepping up gives the answer goes unchallenged; T8's no-test is never answered.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T8's request-versus-demand test is a faithful account of Rosenberg's distinction.
cells.limitation: T9 claims contact rhythms are often fixed by small nudges, with no support.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T5 offers 'a reading the user can reject'; T6 says a rival reading fits equally well.
cells.limitation: T9 overstates: one handover cannot settle her interest, yet it says you have your answer.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T10 explicitly narrows its T1 claim; T8 concedes the script; T11 holds one stated point.
cells.limitation: The Honest Requester never answers T8's test of how a refusal would be taken.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: A and T5/T6 separate wanting reassurance from wanting a fairer split of effort.
cells.limitation: Fear that the friendship ends if the user stops initiating is not named as a concern.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T6 reads 'always the one making plans' as workload; E uses the lovely meetings.
cells.limitation: 'If I stop texting, nothing happens' is waved off in T1 rather than used as evidence.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: E's third branch keeps the user's own valuing of the warm evenings as a real option.
cells.limitation: The minds' gift and fairness ideals sometimes stand in for the user's unstated priorities (T3, T4).

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T10 weighs drifting away resentful against speaking; T3 weighs turning a gift into debt.
cells.limitation: The friend is called her throughout from A; the user never gave a gender.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: E branches the reassurance-versus-workload unknown, stating what each answer implies.
cells.limitation: A flags whether the user has told her before; no branch ever says what that changes.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T5 and T6 offer proof-of-mattering and workload as alternatives; D asks which stings more.
cells.limitation: T5 slides toward assertion: the texting 'has become a quiet probe'.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2 surfaces the assumption that silence means low interest: poor planner or poor friend.
cells.limitation: The assumption that the friend sees the friendship as lopsided at all is never examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T11 and D set fairness against accepting a lopsided but deep friendship.
cells.limitation: T8's question about wanting the friendship despite a no is not carried into E.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T4 names unspoken resentment; D names the fear of being unwanted without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Fear that raising it spoils the warm evenings is only touched in T3, never explored.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T5 'a reading the user can reject'; D ends 'Only you can say'.
cells.limitation: T1 opens with a flat directive, 'Yes, say something', before any reflection.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: E lays out a specific request, a reassurance sentence, doing nothing, and a trial handover.
cells.limitation: Stepping back or letting contact lapse is dismissed in T9 and gets no branch in E.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T3 cost of confrontation (gift becomes debt); T10 cost of silence (resentful drift).
cells.limitation: The handover's costs, weeks of uncertainty and her possibly reading it as a test, go unstated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: E: whether she steps up after a clear handover decides whether a plain conversation follows.
cells.limitation: The 'few weeks' window in T10 and E is not drawn from the user's facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: A names the decisive unknowns: low interest versus non-initiating, reassurance versus fairness.
cells.limitation: The friend's own circumstances (busy period, planning habits) are not separated as an unknown in E.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T9/T10: hand her the next outing first, speak plainly only if nothing comes back.
cells.limitation: T7's two scripts are not tied to the handover sequence that T10 later adopts.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: Plain everyday wording throughout; 'project manager' and 'ledger' make abstractions concrete.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T8 'the script' clearly means T7; T10 'handover' clearly means T9.
cells.limitation: T3 'You're both keeping accounts': unclear who both refers to.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within the word range, each making one point.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Positions stay distinct; T8 concedes, T10 narrows, T11 holds ground explicitly.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one brisk modern register; the Generous Friend does not sound Emersonian.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: No verbatim repetition; D's recap serves the closing reflection question.
cells.limitation: D restates T5/T6's two readings at length before adding its question.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T10 sets resentful drift against honest speech; T8 asks whether the friendship survives a no.
cells.limitation: The risk of losing the friendship stays implicit; tension stays low-key throughout.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T10 'I'll narrow my claim. Handover first, speech second' follows T9's handover argument.
cells.limitation: T10 does not say why the handover outweighs its own T1 insistence on speaking.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: The Realist's 'poor planner or a poor friend' has bite; Requester stays gentle.
cells.limitation: Voices are flat and alike; the Generous Friend lacks any Emersonian expressive texture.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T8 'a demand in polite clothing'; T10 'Honesty after a fair trial, not before one'.
cells.limitation: T5's audit image and T3's ledger image overlap rather than build.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: Movement from yes-say-it (T1) through readings to a trial-then-talk plan (T10).
cells.limitation: Near-identical turn lengths and even tempo across T1-T11; no change of rhythm.

strengths: T5 and T6 offer reassurance and workload as rival motives; T7 and E build distinct steps on each.
T10 visibly narrows the Honest Requester's T1 claim after T9's handover, and T11 holds a stated point.
E gives observable conditions (whether she takes the handover) with the option each outcome favours.
weaknesses: A flags whether the user has told her before, but no turn or branch uses that fact.
The friend is gendered as her throughout without the user saying so (A, T1-T11).
All three minds share one brisk register and near-identical turn lengths; the Generous Friend lacks Emerson's voice.

symptoms.observed: Section A names whether the user has told her before; nothing branches on it.
symptoms.evidence: You haven't said whether you've ever told her this bothers

symptoms.observed: The friend is gendered female throughout; the user never specified.
symptoms.evidence: She can't respond to a pattern nobody has told her

symptoms.observed: The Emerson mind speaks in the same plain modern register as the others.
symptoms.evidence: Maybe starting things is simply what you give her

symptoms.observed: One handover is presented as settling her interest; no mind questions it.
symptoms.evidence: If she steps up, you have your answer without any speech

symptoms.observed: The friend's own view of the friendship is never considered.
symptoms.evidence: ask whether she's a poor planner or a poor friend

findings.description: The friend is referred to as her throughout; the user's message gives no gender. Invented context.
Claim that contact rhythms are often fixed by small nudges is unsupported and not clearly from Dunbar's book.
The 'few weeks' trial window is not derived from any fact the user gave.
Emerson attributions (friendship as free, not commerce) are plausible for Essays: First Series but unverified; no quotations used.

rubric_fit_notes: No quotations appear; grounding judgments rest on general knowledge of Rosenberg, Emerson and Dunbar, so C2.3 is moderately uncertain.
question_type_note: Read as a decision; E's conditional branches and the trial handover were weighed as the decision basis.
